method.cpu_note: Go runtime threads can make process CPU time exceed wall time; CPU time is not energy
method.cpu_source: wait4 rusage (user + system CPU time of the child process); cpu_total is their per-sample sum
method.cross_decode: each frame is decoded by the other implementation and compared with the same expected bytes
method.execution: one CLI process per encode and per decode for both implementations
method.library_comparison: no library harness is used in this court; the existing in-process Rust codec receipt uses a different corpus and is not directly comparable
method.limits: both CLIs use the default normative Limits; no limit flag is set
method.process_overhead: measured separately with --help; not subtracted from encode/decode wall times
method.units: wall/cpu values are nanoseconds; maxrss values are KiB
method.verification: every timed decode is compared byte-for-byte with the fixture before its sample is accepted
method.wall_includes: process spawn, dynamic loading, argument parsing, file I/O, and codec work

notes: Both contestants are CLI processes; no library harness is used, so wall times include a constant process overhead measured separately.
CPU user/sys is CPU time, not energy. No perf counters or RAPL reading is claimed.
TENSOR and TOKENS expected bytes are the raw payload and the canonical token payload respectively; both implementations must decode to the same bytes.
Cross-decode is re-checked here for every frame; it is performance evidence, not a conformance court.
No result is extrapolated to a different corpus, mount, or machine.
